# Viewer IFC · BCF

> Free and open-source IFC and BCF viewer that runs entirely in the browser. Open and federate IFC models, review BCF issues and Solibri reports, inspect elements and their property sets, slice with a section box, edit properties in the 3D view and re-export an updated IFC. Open IFC4x3 road and infrastructure alignments with a 3D axis, an interactive vertical profile, an orthogonal cross-section and a top-down minimap. 100% client-side: models never leave the user's computer — no upload, no account, no server.

Key facts:
- License: GNU AGPL-3.0 (open source).
- Privacy by design: IFC parsing happens locally in the browser via web-ifc (WebAssembly). No file is uploaded; no account or tracking.
- Single-file app: plain HTML/CSS/JS, no framework, no build step. Dependencies (three.js, web-ifc) are loaded from a CDN on first launch.
- Supported formats: IFC2x3, IFC4, IFC4x3, BCF, Solibri report.
- It is a coordination viewer, not just a visualization viewer: federation, BCF issue review, property editing (including bulk) and IFC re-export.
- Infrastructure (IFC4x3): reads IfcAlignment and draws the 3D axis, an interactive vertical/elevation profile, a cross-section orthogonal to the axis (cut or slab, draggable along the chainage in 3D or on the profile) and a top-down minimap of the alignments.
- Author: Alessandro Perugini (BIM Coordinator).
- Bilingual interface: Italian and English.

## Pages

- [Landing page](https://viewifc.com/): overview, features, privacy model and links.
- [Viewer (the app)](https://viewifc.com/viewer/): the in-browser IFC/BCF viewer itself.
- [Guide](https://viewifc.com/guide/): quick-start, how to load models, navigate, open BCF, work on issues and edit parameters.

## Tools

Companion tools that run entirely in the browser (no upload, no install), in the same client-side, privacy-by-design spirit as the viewer.

- [Tools index](https://viewifc.com/tools/): the index page of all the tools — the fourteen available ones plus the roadmap of the upcoming one (BCF → Excel) — filterable by topic, in grid or list density. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Class Patcher](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-class-patcher/): bulk-reclassifies IFC elements from an Excel mapping (Class → IFC entity → ENUMTYPE). For each element matched by a configurable reference property (auto-suggested from the loaded IFC) it rewrites both the IFC class (the STEP entity keyword, e.g. IFCBUILDINGELEMENTPROXY → IFCKERB) and the PredefinedType. The user loads an IFC file and an Excel mapping, picks which columns to use, and downloads a corrected IFC. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Progressiva Converter](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-progressiva-converter/): converts road chainage (progressiva) values stored on IFC elements between plain metres and the kilometric format K+MMM,CC (e.g. 1+234,56), in both directions — metres → text (IFCTEXT) and back to a number (IFCREAL). The user picks which properties to convert (auto-suggested from the loaded IFC). Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Alignment to LandXML](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-alignment-to-landxml/): extracts the IfcAlignment entities from an IFC4x3 file and exports them as LandXML 1.2 — horizontal geometry (Line/Curve/Spiral clothoid) and vertical profile (PVI/ParaCurve) — ready to load into Dalux. Reads the IFC structure with a lightweight client-side STEP parser; the EPSG code and the coordinate/azimuth conventions are configurable. The user loads an IFC file and downloads a LandXML (.xml). Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Split / Extractor](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-split/): the inverse of IFC Merge — extracts a subset of an IFC file, or splits it into several files. The user ticks what to keep in the spatial tree (storeys, buildings, infrastructure parts) or filters by IFC class or by Pset property value; a reference closure filters instead of copying, so types, materials, property sets, openings and nested assembly parts follow their elements with no dangling references and unchanged STEP ids. Output: one reduced .ifc, or several .ifc in a .zip grouped by storey, class or Pset value. A coverage diagnostic reports any part of the file unreachable from the spatial structure, recoverable in a _Rest file. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Merge](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-merge/): merges multiple IFC files into a single federated model — one IfcProject (from the first file, which keeps its whole spatial structure) and one dedicated IfcSite per additional file, named after the file. Copies elements with their geometry, placements, openings, property sets, types, materials, classifications and colours; remaps STEP ids and regenerates duplicate GlobalIds. The user loads two or more IFC files, orders them, and downloads a federated IFC. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Georeference Editor](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-georeference/): reads every place an IFC can declare where it is — IfcMapConversion (+IfcProjectedCRS), the site RefLatitude/RefLongitude and the TrueNorth of the geometric context — flags disagreements and degenerate cases (e.g. the Navisworks xa=xo=0 MapConversion), and rewrites the three slots consistent. The origin can be set by picking the trusted slot, dragging on a metric-grid plan, entering two known points or pasting a coordinate pair; coordinate conversions (ETRS89/WGS84 UTM, RDN2008, Gauss-Boaga, DHDN Gauss-Krüger, OSGB) run entirely client-side. Geometry is untouched: only the declaration entities are byte-patched, STEP ids unchanged. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Data Extractor](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-data-extractor/): brings the properties and quantities of an IFC file into a spreadsheet (.xlsx with one sheet per IFC class, or a single .csv). The user builds the column schema from a catalogue of everything found in the file — direct attributes, instance Psets, type Psets, quantities with their unit — and every column declares its coverage: on how many rows it is actually filled. Empty cells can be flagged in amber, inherited from the type when missing, or the incomplete rows skipped; rows can be one-per-element, grouped by type or summed by storey. The column schema persists locally and is offered again on the next file, so coverage can be compared across revisions. Read-only: the IFC is never modified. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Diff](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-diff/): compares two revisions of an IFC file by GlobalId — added, removed, modified with the field-by-field (attributes, Pset properties, quantities, absolute position from the placement chain, geometry) — net of re-export noise: OwnerHistory ignored (toggle), STEP #id renumbering ignored by construction (structural geometry fingerprint, numbers normalised to 6 significant digits), position tolerance 0/1/5 mm. Orphans (recreated elements whose GlobalId changed) are re-matched by class+geometry+position+name with a confidence score: pairs ≥ 0.90 automatically, lower ones proposed for manual confirmation. Output: a multi-sheet .xlsx report, or a BCF 2.1 .bcfzip with one topic per class × change type. The noise rules persist locally, so counts stay comparable across issues. Read-only: neither IFC is modified. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Health Check](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-health-check/): runs twenty-eight checks on an IFC file before it is handed over, and deliberately produces no overall score. Each check declares three things: its real severity (blocks the delivery / to fix / observation), the count as a problem rather than as elements (4,000 unclassified walls are one wrong export setting, so every check carries its root causes), and who fixes it — authoring, export or mapping — with the concrete upstream correction. The checks cover file structure (schema and MVD, units, spatial hierarchy, elements outside it, dangling references, header, storey elevations), identity (duplicate and malformed GlobalIds, classification, generic names, proxies, types), geometry (distance from the origin, georeferencing, nested boolean depth, surface-only bodies with no computable volume, missing representations, overlapping duplicates, heavy tessellation) and data (missing Psets, quantities and materials, placeholder values, contradictory same-named properties, unnamed spaces, empty Psets). Severities and thresholds are editable and persist locally. A second view, the delivery gate, turns the blocking checks — plus the client's brief loaded as an IDS file, evaluated with the same engine as the viewer — into pass/fail requirements; a blocker can be waived only with a written reason and a name, and the waiver is declared and counted separately, never as compliance. Output: a PDF report (written without any library) or a BCF 2.1 .bcfzip with one topic per check. Read-only: the IFC is never modified. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Pset Editor](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-pset-editor/): fills in the missing properties of an IFC by condition rather than element by element. A rule reads "every external load-bearing IfcWall → Pset_WallCommon.FireRating = EI 90" and declares by itself how many elements it touches, how many already carried a value, and what it does on a conflict (leave it / overwrite / ask, with conflicts grouped by their current value); rule order is priority. Conditions can test the IFC class, any Pset property or quantity, name, description, ObjectType, type name or storey, or come from an .xlsx sheet matched on GlobalId. A second view puts the same editing on a 3D selection: pick elements in the model, colour by property value or by missing property, and edit a multi-selection with different values ("3 different values" → make uniform, or touch only the blanks); every edit lands in an undoable change log. Values are typed: the IFC type is inferred first from the file itself, then from the standard Pset catalogue, and a value that does not hold the type (the classic "yes" into an IfcBoolean) is rejected before export, not after. Shared IfcPropertySets are split rather than rewritten in place, so elements outside the selection are never changed; quantities are read-only. Output: the written .ifc, a .json rulebook that reapplies unchanged to the next issue, and a .csv change log — the file itself carries no provenance marking. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC IDS Editor](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-ids-editor/): creates and edits buildingSMART IDS 1.0 files entirely in the browser — open an existing .ids and modify it, or write one from scratch. Full file header (title, copyright, version, description, author, date, purpose, milestone) and, per specification, identifier, IFC versions, instructions and relevance (required / optional / prohibited, encoded as the applicability minOccurs/maxOccurs). All six facet types of the standard — entity, attribute, property, classification, material, partOf — are available both as applicability and as requirements, each value with five comparison modes (exact value, enumeration, XSD pattern, numeric range, length) mapped to xs:restriction; requirement facets carry their cardinality per the official XSD (entity always required, partOf without optional). The distinctive part is the live test: drop an .ifc and every specification declares how many elements it catches and how many fail, while you type — a specification that catches nobody is flagged red as a false green (in any checker it is indistinguishable from a perfect model) and challenged before export. The property data type proposes itself from the property's nominal type in the test model, then from the standard Pset catalogue, and a declared type that contradicts the file is flagged. Classifications, materials and properties can also be picked from the online bSDD dictionary (the only network call on the whole site; only the search text is sent). A second view generates specifications in bulk from the data-model table (.xlsx or .csv, long or wide form): classes in rows, parameters in columns, one rule with placeholders, reviewed as a matrix where each cell is required/optional/prohibited/absent (click to cycle, drag to set many), with per-class element counts on the test model; regenerating after a table revision preserves hand-edited specifications and flags them. Parser and evaluator are the same module as the viewer's IDS checks, so what the editor writes is exactly what the viewer verifies — round trip guaranteed by tests. Output: the .ids file (schema-ordered, escaped, with schemaLocation) and a PDF sheet of the brief with the test outcomes. The test model never ends up in the file. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [LandXML → IFC4x3](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-landxml-to-ifc/): the opposite direction of IFC Alignment to LandXML — the surveyor's LandXML alignment becomes IfcAlignment entities in IFC4X3_ADD2, either inserted into an existing model (IFC4x3 directly; an IFC2X3 or IFC4 host is migrated to IFC4X3_ADD2 in the same output — targeted per-line rewrite with unchanged ids and a declared table: optional attributes padded, removed entities renamed, DoorStyle/WindowStyle converted to types, classification dates turned into strings, style assignments flattened; unmapped removed types stay as they were and are counted) or written as a fresh file with its own IfcMapConversion. The host byte-patch is otherwise purely additive: original ids untouched, units and MapConversion rotation of the host respected. IFC4x3 wants two truths that must coincide — the business logic (parametric segments: lines, circular arcs, clothoids) and the geometric curve that follows from them (IfcCompositeCurve + IfcGradientCurve): both are generated and checked against each other, and the export stops if they diverge beyond 1 mm. Junctions that do not close (rounded coordinates in the source file) are shown on the axis with their position/tangent gap against the tolerance (1 mm · 0.001 gon): sew onto the computed chain (default), refit the clothoid between both ends, or leave the discontinuity declared and export it as BCF topics. Non-clothoid spirals (bloss, cosine, sinusoid, biquadratic) are open cases decided in the open: an equivalent clothoid slid between the adjacent elements (curvature-continuous, downstream axis untouched, deviation computed from the true curvature law), a faithful polyline, or stop and ask upstream. Station equations become IfcReferent (STATION) with Pset_Stationing. The choices are recorded in the file as Pset_Conversione (toggleable). Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC schema change](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-schema-change/): rewrites the same model in another IFC schema version — IFC2X3/IFC4 upwards to IFC4X3_ADD2, IFC4X3 downwards to IFC2X3 or IFC4 (4X1/4X2 accepted as declared intermediate stops; 2X2 read with the 2X3 table, declared). Targeted per-line rewrite: entity ids and GlobalIds unchanged, everything not in the table stays byte-identical. Schema knowledge is extracted from web-ifc (the same parser the viewer uses): class existence and argument counts per version, plus a demotion map computed by walking the inheritance tree to the first instantiable landing that exists in the target (MEP occurrences fall onto the 2x3 Flow families, the rest onto IfcBuildingElementProxy/Type with the original class recorded in ObjectType, e.g. "IfcKerb.RIGID"). Going up nothing is lost: optional attributes padded, retired classes renamed (DoorStyle→DoorType, classification dates to strings, style assignments flattened), generic IfcBuildingElementProxy boxes can take their real IFC4X3 class (IfcKerb/IfcPavement/IfcCourse/IfcEarthworks*) by IT/EN keyword recognition — all, none, or group by group — and IfcSite+Building+Storey can be promoted to IfcRoad/IfcRoadPart. Going down the losses are listed before the file: the IfcAlignment tree disappears as logic (linear placements become absolute coordinates, evaluated on the business segments or taken from CartesianPosition), tessellations become IfcFacetedBrep and indexed polycurves become polylines (arcs discretised, sagitta ≤ 2 mm, declared), IfcMapConversion/CRS are lost but E/N/H stay in the register, a missing IfcOwnerHistory is generated and declared. Whatever has no safe map stays as it was — counted and declared, never converted at random (IfcSectionedSolidHorizontal bodies included, v1). Output: the new .ifc (original untouched), a conversion register .csv listing every changed entity with the way back, and an optional Pset_Conversione on the IfcProject. STEP header rewritten with the target FILE_SCHEMA and a declared ViewDefinition. A second view checks the change: losses grouped by cause and the sample element read field by field, before and after. Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [IFC Site Context](https://viewifc.com/tools/ifc-site-context/): draw an area on a map (rectangle or polygon, up to 10 km², or a square from centre coordinates) — or start from your own project IFC, or a route (drawn, GeoJSON, KML, DXF or the model's IfcAlignment axes) buffered into a corridor whose band area counts against the limit — and download a georeferenced IFC context model (plus a LandXML 1.2 TIN of the terrain) — terrain, LoD1 buildings, roads and water from open data — to federate with design models. Terrain from the national bare-earth DTM where one exists — swissALTI3D (swisstopo), AHN (PDOK), TINITALY 1.1 (INGV), RGE ALTI (IGN), USGS 3DEP — fetched in pieces with a minimal in-browser GeoTIFF/BIL reader, holes (under buildings, on water) filled from neighbours; elsewhere, and where the national service does not answer, from AWS Terrain Tiles (Terrarium, z15): the source under each tile (EU-DEM, SRTM, USGS 3DEP, UK LIDAR, …) is read from the tile headers and declared with its nominal resolution, vertical datum and licence; surface models (EU-DEM, SRTM: they include buildings and vegetation) are flagged with IsSurfaceModel and a warning, isolated SRTM voids are despiked, and an experimental option lowers the terrain under building footprints. Adaptive TIN (Delatin) with a vertical tolerance (auto 0.5 m, 1 m on SRTM) clipped exactly to the drawn polygon, as a surface or a closed solid with vertical walls. Buildings from Overture Maps GeoParquet read directly in the browser with range requests (no server, no DuckDB): footprints with courtyards, based on the minimum of the written terrain under their vertices so none floats, height chain SOURCE (OSM or Microsoft ML estimate, named in HeightSource) → FROM_LEVELS → AREA_MEDIAN (footprints ≥ 50 m², ≥ 20 samples) → DEFAULT, always recorded. IFC4 (default), IFC4X3_ADD2 or IFC2X3; georeferencing mode A (IfcMapConversion + IfcProjectedCRS, local coordinates around a rounded origin) or B (map coordinates in placements; default for IFC2X3, which gets ePSet_MapConversion/ePSet_ProjectedCRS). Start from a model: the project IFC is read in the browser with web-ifc (it never leaves it); its IfcMapConversion + IfcProjectedCRS, IFC2x3 ePSet_MapConversion/ePSet_ProjectedCRS or large map coordinates in placements give the CRS, origin, rotation, TrueNorth and georeferencing mode, its footprint plus a margin becomes the proposed area, and the context is written in the same local system so it overlaps the project at the first try; "open in the viewer" hands over project and context together. A model that is not georeferenced is reported as such. CRS: the UTM zone of the area by default, or any metric projected EPSG (common ones bundled, others looked up on epsg.io — only the code leaves the browser), with the grid scale factor checked. Roads, paths and squares, railways and water from OpenStreetMap via the OpenFreeMap vector tiles (OpenMapTiles schema, z14, the same tiles as the map): one surface per family, laid on the written terrain 15–24 cm above it, default widths by class (declared: OSM rarely has real widths), bridges as separate decks linear from abutment to abutment, tunnels and indoor ways left out, sea at 0 m, lakes flat at the water level, rivers at the water level rather than on the embankment. Terrain as IfcGeographicElement TERRAIN (IfcTriangulatedFaceSet), roads/paths/railways/water as IfcGeographicElement USERDEFINED (CONTEXT_ROAD, CONTEXT_PATH, CONTEXT_RAIL, CONTEXT_WATER), buildings as IfcBuildingElementProxy USERDEFINED/CONTEXT_BUILDING — never IfcBuilding, so the context does not pollute the project's spatial structure. Deterministic GlobalIds (from the Overture GERS id): regenerating the same area gives the same GUIDs. Every element carries a ViewIFC_Provenance property set (source, id, release, licence, height and method, retrieval date); the site carries generator, CRS, grid scale factor, attributions and disclaimer. A published IDS lists what every file guarantees. Report before download (buildings per height method, terrain source/resolution/datum, triangles, file size, licences), download or "open in the viewer" without re-uploading. The area is sent only to the data providers (map tiles, terrain, buildings, and Nominatim search if used), never to viewifc.com. Buildings data ODbL 1.0 (derivative database: share-alike if published). Bilingual (Italian/English).
- [Terrain Sculptor](https://viewifc.com/tools/terrain-sculptor/): sculpt a topography in the browser and export it for Revit and Rhino. The terrain is a height grid (up to ~4 million nodes, e.g. 1×1 km at 0.5 m) started flat, sloped or rolling, or read from a LandXML TIN (Civil 3D, IFC Site Context), a GeoTIFF or ESRI ASCII grid, or x,y,z survey points (Delaunay), or handed over in one click from IFC Site Context ("Sculpt the terrain" passes its national DTM grid through the browser's storage, never a server); nodes outside the survey are filled, hatched and left out of the exports. Brushes (raise, lower, smooth, flatten) shape the ground; pads (polygon at a level) and ramps (axis, width, start and end levels or grade) stay editable objects applied in order on top of it: side slopes (V/H) run between the work's level ± slope × distance, keeping the existing ground inside that band and cutting or filling outside, so the toe finds the terrain by itself, with an optional blend; a ramp started inside a pad hooks onto its edge and follows its level. Cut and fill against the starting terrain, undo/redo, autosave in the browser (IndexedDB). Exports around a declared origin (Revit reads a points file relative to its internal origin): a points CSV for the Revit toposolid (Create from Import › Specify Points File) with a 10k (every version), 20k or 50k budget, chosen by Delatin and then made robust so the stated vertical error holds whichever Delaunay diagonals Revit picks among cocircular grid points (on the sample terrain a naive re-triangulation cut the pad edge by 14.5 cm; robust: 1.0 cm); a Rhino 7/8 .3dm in metres (cubic NURBS surface with control points on the Greville abscissae refined by progressive iterative approximation, contours and index contours, an adaptive TIN mesh with UVs, a closed volume, the Revit points, each on its own layer); an OBJ with quads and UVs. It also opens the Revit toposolid from an IFC (IfcGeographicElement .TERRAIN., in the project's internal coordinates, so the CSV lands back on top of it), shows the building IFC as a reference model, and saves a lossless .terrain project with the editable works. Works also include sloped pads (level at the centre, draining towards an azimuth), ramps with a locked grade whose end moves by itself, banks between a crest level and a toe level, and different side slopes in cut and in fill. A scale-model view gives the block solid sides and water bodies drawn as outlines that never rise above their lowest spill point (water goes to the .3dm on its own layer). Analysis maps show slopes over a limit and cut and fill; a slope-limit brush and a whole-terrain command (Lipschitz envelope on a 5×5 chamfer distance, worked at the limit × cos π/8 so that no node exceeds it on the map) cut, fill or balance; locked areas are left alone by brushes and by the limit; earthworks are reported work by work. The .3dm closed volume has its own vertices for top, walls and bottom (sharp edges), vertical quad walls and a quad grid bottom. Bilingual (Italian/English).

## Tech stack

- Rendering: three.js 0.160.0 (MIT).
- IFC parsing: web-ifc 0.0.77 (MPL-2.0), WebAssembly.
- Fonts: Barlow Semi Condensed, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono.
